source_text:
Ὃς ἂν οὑν ἐλθὼν διδάξῃ ὑμᾶς ταῦτα πάντα τὰ προειρημένα, δέξασθε αὐτόν:
ἐὰν δὲ αὐτὸς ὁ διδάσκων στραφεὶς διδάσκῃ ἄλλην διδαχὴν εἰς τὸ καταλῦσαι, μὴ αὐτοῦ ἀκούσητε: εἰς δὲ τὸ προσθεῖναι δικαιοσύνην καὶ γνῶσιν κυρίου, δέξασθε αὐτὸν ὡς κύριον.
Περὶ δὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων καὶ προφητῶν, κατὰ τὸ δόγμα τοῦ εὐαγγελίου οὕτω ποιήσατε.
πᾶς δὲ ἀπόστολος ἐρχόμενος πρὸς ὑμᾶς δεχθήτω ὡς κύριος:
οὐ μενεῖ δὲ εἰ μὴ ἡμέραν μίαν: ἐὰν δὲ ᾖ χρεία, καὶ τὴν ἄλλην: τρεῖς δὲ ἐὰν μείνῃ, ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστίν.
ἐξερχόμενος δὲ ὁ ἀπόστολος μηδὲν λαμβανέτω εἰ μὴ ἄρτον, ἕως οὖ αὐλισθῇ: ἐὰν δὲ ἀργύριον αἰτῇ, ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί.
Καὶ πάντα προφήτην λαλοῦντα ἐν πνεύματι οὐ πειράσετε οὐδὲ διακρινεῖτε: πᾶσα γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφεθήσεται, αὕτη δὲ ἡ ἁμαρτία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται.
οὐ πᾶς δὲ ὁ λαλῶν ἐν πνεύματι προφήτης ἐστίν, ἀλλ’ ἐὰν ἔχῃ τοὺς τρόπους κυρίου. ἀπὸ οὖν τῶν τρόπων γνωσθήσεται ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης καὶ ὁ προφήτης.
καὶ πᾶς προφήτης ὁρίζων τράπεζαν ἐν πνεύματι οὐ φάγεται ἀπ’ αὐτῆς, εἰ δὲ μήγε ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί.
πᾶς δὲ προφήτης διδάσκων τὴν ἀλήθειαν, εἰ ἃ διδάσκει οὐ ποιεῖ. ψευδοπροφήτης ἐστί.
πᾶς δὲ προφήτης δεδοκιμασμένος, ἀληθινός, ποιῶν εἰς μυστήριον κοσμικὸν ἐκκλησίας, μὴ διδάσκων δὲ ποιεῖν, ὅσα αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, οὐ κριθήσεται ἐφ̓ ὑμῶν: μετὰ θεοῦ γὰρ ἔχει τὴν κρίσιν: ὡσαύτως γὰρ ἐποίησαν καὶ οἱ ἀρχαῖοι προφῆται.
ὃς δ’ ἂν εἴπῃ ἐν πνεύματι: δός μοι ἀργύρια ἢ ἕτερά τινα, οὐκ ἀκούσεσθε αὐτοῦ: ἐὰν δὲ περὶ ἄλλων ὑστερούντων εἴπῃ δοῦναι, μηδεὶς αὐτὸν κρινέτω.
thought_title: Testing traveling teachers, apostles, and prophets
orientation: The anonymous author of the Didache is giving the community rules for receiving and testing traveling Christian teachers, apostles, and prophets.
pass_a_gloss: Whoever then comes and teaches you all these things said before, receive him. But if the teacher himself turns and teaches another teaching, so as to destroy, do not listen to him; but if he teaches so as to add righteousness and knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord. Now concerning the apostles and prophets, according to the decree of the gospel, do thus. Let every apostle who comes to you be received as the Lord. He shall not stay except one day; but if there is need, also the next; but if he stays three days, he is a false prophet. When the apostle leaves, let him take nothing except bread, until he lodges; but if he asks for money, he is a false prophet. And every prophet speaking in the Spirit you shall not test or judge; for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven. Not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet, but only if he has the ways of the Lord. Therefore from the ways the false prophet and the prophet will be known. And every prophet who orders a table in the Spirit shall not eat from it; otherwise he is a false prophet. Every prophet who teaches the truth, if he does not do what he teaches, is a false prophet. Every prophet who has been tested, genuine, acting for an earthly mystery of the church, but not teaching others to do what he himself does, shall not be judged by you; for he has his judgment with God; for the ancient prophets also acted in the same way. Whoever says in the Spirit: give me money or certain other things, you shall not listen to him; but if he says to give on behalf of others who are in need, let no one judge him.

choices.why: Keeps the glossary term 'teaching' for διδαχή and preserves the contrast with the teaching already received.
Renders the purpose infinitive literally, preserving the destructive intent of the false teaching.

choices.english: according to the decree of the gospel
choices.why: Keeps δόγμα as 'decree' to show the gospel is treated as an authoritative ruling, not just a story.
rejected: according to the teaching of the gospel

choices.why: Uses 'ways' to echo the Two Ways framework of the work and keeps the plural τρόπους as concrete patterns of behavior.

choices.english: an earthly mystery of the church
choices.why: Renders the difficult phrase literally, preserving the oddity of 'earthly mystery' rather than smoothing it into a familiar idiom.
rejected: a worldly mystery of the church
a symbolic act for the church

choices.why: Uses the glossary term consistently throughout the section.

bible_refs.note: πᾶσα γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφεθήσεται, αὕτη δὲ ἡ ἁμαρτία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται

pass_b_english: So if someone comes and teaches you everything just described, receive him. But if the teacher himself turns aside and teaches another teaching so as to destroy, do not listen to him. If he teaches so as to add righteousness and knowledge of the Lord, receive him as the Lord.

Concerning apostles and prophets, act according to the decree of the gospel. Every apostle who comes to you is to be received as the Lord. He is not to stay more than one day; if there is need, he may stay a second. But if he stays three days, he is a false prophet. When an apostle leaves, he is to take nothing except bread until he finds lodging. If he asks for money, he is a false prophet.

Do not test or judge any prophet speaking in the Spirit, for every sin will be forgiven, but the sin against the Spirit will not be forgiven. Not everyone who speaks in the Spirit is a prophet, but only if he has the ways of the Lord. So the false prophet and the prophet will be known by their ways. Any prophet who commands in the Spirit that a table be set must not eat from it; if he does, he is a false prophet. Any prophet who teaches the truth but does not do what he teaches is a false prophet. But any prophet who has been tested and is true, who performs an earthly mystery of the church but does not teach others to do what he himself does, is not to be judged by you; his judgment is with God. The ancient prophets acted in the same way. If anyone says in the Spirit, "Give me money or something else," do not listen to him. But if he tells you to give to others who are in need, let no one judge him.

problems.source_quote: πᾶσα γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφεθήσεται, αὕτη δὲ ἡ ἁμαρτία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται
problems.why: The allusion is to the unforgivable sin saying, but Didache lacks 'against the Spirit'; Matthew 12:31 is imprecise.

edits.old: but this sin will not be forgiven (Matthew 12:31).
edits.new: but this sin will not be forgiven (Matthew 12:31–32).

problems.source_quote: πᾶσα γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφεθήσεται, αὕτη δὲ ἡ ἁμαρτία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται
problems.why: The Didache quotes/blasphemy against the Spirit saying, but Matthew 12:31-32 speaks of blasphemy against the Spirit; Mark 3:28-29 is closer to the exact wording.

edits.old: but this sin will not be forgiven (Matthew 12:31–32).
edits.new: but this sin will not be forgiven (Mark 3:28–29).

fixed: Changed the scripture reference from Matthew 12:31–32 to Mark 3:28–29, which more closely matches the Didache's wording about every sin being forgiven except the sin against the Spirit.

problems.source_quote: πᾶσα γὰρ ἁμαρτία ἀφεθήσεται, αὕτη δὲ ἡ ἁμαρτία οὐκ ἀφεθήσεται
problems.why: The Didache quotes this without attribution; adding 'Mark 3:28-29' is an editorial addition not in source.

edits.old: but this sin will not be forgiven (Mark 3:28–29).
edits.new: but this sin will not be forgiven.

fixed: Removed the parenthetical citation (Mark 3:28–29) as an editorial addition not present in the source.

problems.why: Term for a fraudulent visitor shifts from 'false prophet' to 'religious profiteer' without signal.

problems.quote: for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven
problems.why: Unclear if this is the author's own teaching or a citation of the Lord's saying (cf. Matt 12:31).
problems.fix: Mark as allusion: 'as the Lord said (cf. Matthew 12:31)'.

edits.old: for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven.
edits.new: for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven, as the Lord said (Matthew 12:31).

fixed: The glossary problem about 'religious profiteer' does not apply to this section; the English consistently uses 'false prophet' for ψευδοπροφήτης, and 'religious profiteer' does not appear here.
The speaker problem was real: the saying about the unforgivable sin is an allusion to the Lord's teaching, so I marked it as such with a Matthew 12:31 reference.

problems.quote: Any prophet who orders a table in the Spirit must not eat from it; if he does, he is a false prophet.
problems.why: Phrase “orders a table in the Spirit” is unintelligible.
problems.fix: Replace with “any prophet who sets a table for himself in the Spirit”.

edits.old: Any prophet who orders a table in the Spirit must not eat from it; if he does, he is a false prophet.
edits.new: Any prophet who sets a table in the Spirit must not eat from it; if he does, he is a false prophet.

problems.quote: Do not test or judge any prophet speaking in the Spirit, for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven
problems.why: It is ambiguous whether this is the author’s rule, a quoted authority, or a prophetic voice.
problems.fix: Attribute the statement, e.g., “The apostolic teaching instructs”.

problems.quote: for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven
problems.why: Self‑contradictory clause makes the rule unintelligible.
problems.fix: Revise to: “All sins are forgiven except blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.”

problems.quote: for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven, as the Lord said (Matthew 12:31)
problems.why: Matthew 12:31 does not contain this wording; it speaks of blasphemy against the Holy Spirit.
problems.fix: Replace with the proper verse or adjust wording to reflect the actual verse.

edits.old: Do not test or judge any prophet speaking in the Spirit, for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven, as the Lord said (Matthew 12:31).
edits.new: Do not test or judge any prophet speaking in the Spirit, for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven.

edits.old: for every sin will be forgiven, but this sin will not be forgiven.
edits.new: for every sin will be forgiven, but the sin against the Spirit will not be forgiven.

fixed: Removed the incorrect Matthew 12:31 citation and clarified the unforgivable sin as the sin against the Spirit, matching the source's contrast between general sins and this particular sin.

last_rejected.quote: if he does, he is a false prophet
last_rejected.why: Source says 'if not, he is a false prophet' — i.e., if he does NOT eat, he is false. English reverses the condition.
last_rejected.fix: if he does not, he is a false prophet
last_rejected.ruling: εἰ δὲ μήγε = 'but if not' (i.e., if he eats), standard Greek idiom. English 'if he does' correctly captures this.

last_rejected.why: αὐλισθῇ means 'spends the night' or 'lodges,' not 'finds lodging'—the verb is intransitive, not transitive.
last_rejected.fix: until he lodges for the night
last_rejected.ruling: αὐλισθῇ means 'spend the night'; 'until he finds lodging' conveys this adequately in context, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: who performs an earthly mystery of the church
last_rejected.why: κοσμικόν here means 'worldly' in sense of pertaining to the world/order of creation, not 'earthly'; 'cosmic' or 'of the world' is meant.
last_rejected.fix: who performs a mystery of the world-order of the church
last_rejected.ruling: κοσμικόν can mean 'earthly/worldly'; 'earthly' is within normal range, not a major mistranslation.

polish.changed: Clarified the obscure phrase about a prophet commanding a table to be set, made the speaker and pronoun references explicit, and smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud while preserving every claim and Scripture reference.

notes.quote: Any prophet who orders a table in the Spirit must not eat from it; if he does, he is a false prophet.
notes.why: Phrase “orders a table in the Spirit” is unintelligible.
notes.fix: Replace with “any prophet who sets a table for himself in the Spirit”.
